title: Refusals that talk too much
eyebrow: You pointed at the paragraph agents keep getting shouted at with. Measured: it is mostly wrong, and always too long.

actions.fyi: The interruptions are fixed. Checking whether work actually moves then turned up something worse, also fixed: nine jobs were shut for good.

status.now: The interruptions are fixed and on the main line. So is the reason nine jobs could never be finished.
status.next_up: The nine jobs get their objections back as work anyone can pick up, once the allowance resets at 4pm.

The nudge is one short line, once, instead of a paragraph seven times
All of it carried onto the shared copy the tools are moving to

content.lead: Your figure for what refusals cost is nine times too high.

blocks.text: Of the 216 firings on record, only 24 happened to a real session. The other 192 are the test suite exercising the check, which writes into the same ledger. Any number you have read off it so far was inflated.

content.label: What is fixed and where it stands
content.lead: Three separate ways it interrupted, all closed and all in the main line.

rows: Push a session waiting on a background job or a watcher
leave it alone — proved four ways
Forget a worker existed one turn after it was sent off
count it busy until it reports back
Demand a page link for work a worker did, not the session
ask only the one that finished something
Print 627 characters, up to seven times a turn
print 115, once

blocks.text: Carried onto the shared copy the tools are moving to, so the move cannot quietly undo it. That project's whole suite is green.

Unfinished: the tests. The worker writing them ran out of the account's allowance mid-job, so its half-written work sits in a copy on disk waiting for 4pm. Nothing is lost and nothing is broken by leaving it.

content.label: You asked whether work actually moves. It did not
content.lead: Nine jobs were shut for good, and had been for hours.

tiles.key: objections thrown away, one job alone

blocks.text: A finished job is read by an outsider, and what it objects to becomes work you can see. The reader is told to keep file names out of the line you read and put them alongside. It then pasted them back into that line — and the board refuses a line written in builder's words. So every objection about code was thrown away, the reading never closed, and the job could never be finished or called off.

Watched, not argued: the same objection was offered to the board twice, once with the location in that line and once without. Refused, then accepted. The accepted one is now a real piece of work under the job that was stuck.
Fixed in every copy on disk. The shared home the tools are moving to never had it, so the move settles it permanently. What is left is giving the nine jobs their thrown-away objections back.

decisions.title: The rule itself stays
decisions.why: It is doing what you asked for — you are not typing continue any more. What is broken is when it fires and how much it says, not that it exists.

decisions.title: Two pushes instead of seven
decisions.why: Every recorded case that reached seven was a wrong push. If two nudges do not move a session, a third is not going to, and the ceiling is what turns one wrong push into seven.

decisions.title: The reasoning lives in one place
decisions.why: A refusal says what is wrong and what to do. Why the rule exists is handed to every session at the start and written in the board's own notes — a refusal that repeats it is the same words in three places.

decisions.title: Every check gets the same treatment, not just this one
decisions.why: You said all of them, and the count agrees: the stopping one is 6 refusals out of 37 written the same way.

next.if_nothing: The interruptions stay gone, but nine jobs stay shut with their objections lost, and nothing holds either fix in place.

steps.step: The nine shut jobs get their objections back, so they can be finished or called off
Both fixes get tests that go red without them, so they cannot be undone by accident
The remaining refusals become one line, so the screen shows what is wrong instead of an argument
Your cost figures count only what really happened
